## Claims
- [source-backed] The alternate ar5iv full-text record states Theorem 1.2 for bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and proves minimality of the first family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-110]
- [source-backed] The supplied provider text identifies equations (8)–(10), Definition 2.1, and Lemma 2.5, but its mathematical content is visibly truncated at precisely required portions, including the valid-tuple conditions. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 143-189]
- [source-backed] Lemma 4.2 imposes \(N\leq\min(j,n-r-i)\), whereas Theorem 4.4 then treats arbitrary valid tuples by a scaling argument; thus that bound is proof-only, not a theorem hypothesis. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 429-494]
- [source-backed] Theorem 4.5 derives absence of the syzygy from Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 4.4. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 495-502]
- [unsupported] The requested uncorrupted bounded excerpt containing complete equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1’s inequalities was not retrieved from the supplied provider material.

## Strategy
Compared the alternate-provider full text with the required locations and separated Theorem 1.2’s bigrassmannian hypothesis from the temporary Lemma 4.2 bound.

## Gaps
The alternate extraction is corrupted in the required formulas; hence the complete valid-tuple inequalities and exact equations (8)–(10) cannot be transcribed faithfully.
